title: Germany Opportunity Card 2026: Points, Rules & How to Apply
metaDescription: Germany Opportunity Card 2026: score 6+ points, 12-month job search stay, 20 hrs/week work. Points table, blocked account rules and application steps explained.
headline: Germany Opportunity Card (Chancenkarte) 2026: Points & Rules

sections.content:
The Chancenkarte, or Opportunity Card, lets qualified non-EU citizens live in Germany for up to 12 months while searching for a job, without needing an offer first. Card holders may work part-time up to 20 hours per week in any sector and take trial employment of up to two weeks per employer.

Once you find qualified employment, you convert to a standard work residence permit or EU Blue Card. A follow-up Opportunity Card can add up to two more years if you have a qualifying offer but cannot switch permits immediately.
sections.title: What the Opportunity Card Is

sections.content:
There are two routes onto the card. Route one is for recognized skilled workers: if your foreign degree or vocational qualification is fully recognized in Germany, confirmed through the Anabin database or a ZAB Statement of Comparability, you qualify directly with no points needed.

Route two is the points system for partially recognized qualifications. IT professionals with three years of practical experience can use that experience in place of formal recognition. Most self-taught and mid-career applicants take this route.
sections.title: The Two Routes: Recognized Worker vs Points

sections.content:
You need at least 6 points across the categories. Partial qualification recognition gives 4 points, a shortage occupation adds 1, two years of recent experience gives 2 and five years gives 3. German at A2, B1 or B2-plus earns 1, 2 or 3 points, while English at C1 earns 1.

Age under 35 earns 2 points and 35 to 40 earns 1. A prior legal stay of six months in Germany adds 1 point, as does a spouse who also qualifies. Within each category only the highest applicable tier counts, so tiers do not stack.
sections.title: The Points System Explained

sections.content:
Applicants must prove they can support themselves: about 1,091 euros net per month in 2026, shown through a blocked account, a sponsor's declaration of commitment, or a part-time job contract. Health insurance and a clean criminal record are also required.

Applications from outside Germany go through the Federal Foreign Office's Consular Services Portal, while those already in Germany apply at the local Foreigners' Registration Office. Always verify your points with the official Chancenkarte self-check tool before applying.
sections.title: Financial Proof and How to Apply

faqs.a: You need a minimum of 6 points on the Chancenkarte points system, unless you qualify directly as a recognized skilled worker. Points come from qualification recognition, work experience, language skills, age, shortage occupation status, prior stays in Germany and an eligible spouse or partner.
faqs.q: How many points do I need for the Germany Opportunity Card?

faqs.a: Yes, you can qualify with English alone if your other criteria are strong enough. The baseline requirement is German at A1 level or English at B2 level. Higher German levels earn extra points, and English at C1 earns one point, but German is not strictly mandatory.
faqs.q: Do I need to speak German for the Opportunity Card?

faqs.a: You must prove financial self-sufficiency of about 1,091 euros net per month, roughly 13,092 euros for the full year. Acceptable proof includes a blocked account, a formal declaration of commitment from a sponsor in Germany, or a part-time employment contract covering the amount.
faqs.q: How much money do I need to show for the Chancenkarte?

faqs.a: The card is valid for up to 12 months and cannot be renewed just to keep searching. If you secure a qualifying job offer but cannot switch to a standard work permit immediately, a follow-up Opportunity Card can extend your stay by up to two additional years with Federal Employment Agency approval.
